definitions.explanation: An informal suffix used for children, girls, or close friends. Expresses affection or familiarity.

examples.japanese: {花子|はなこ}ちゃん、⟦おはよう→おはよう：05205_ohayou⟧。
⟦うち→内：01328_uchi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{泣|な}く→泣く：00655_naku⟧。
⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{頃|ころ}→〜ころ：03091_koro⟧、⟦みんな→みんな：02972_minna⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧「みいちゃん」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{呼|よ}ばれていた→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧。
examples.english: When I was a child, everyone called me 'Mii-chan.'

notes:
～ちゃん is an affectionate name suffix derived from ～さん. It expresses closeness, cuteness, or endearment.

WHO IT'S USED FOR:
- Children and babies (⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧ = baby)
- Girls and young women
- Close friends (regardless of gender, in casual settings)
- Pets and cute things
- Family in baby talk: ⟦おかあちゃん→お母ちゃん：21588_okaachan⟧ (mommy), ⟦おとうちゃん→おとうちゃん：noentry⟧ (daddy), ⟦おばあちゃん→おばあちゃん：10968_obaachan⟧ (grandma)

NAME SHORTENING:
Names are often shortened before adding ちゃん: {花子|はなこ} → はなちゃん, ゆうこ → ゆうちゃん.

HONORIFIC HIERARCHY:
- ～⟦{様|さま}→様：01549_sama⟧: very formal/respectful
- ～⟦さん→さん：09848_san⟧: polite, general use
- ～⟦{君|くん}→君：01998_kun⟧: informal, mainly for males
- ～ちゃん: affectionate, mainly for females/children

WATCH OUT:
Using ～ちゃん with someone you're not close to can seem presumptuous or condescending. In the workplace, it's generally inappropriate except among very close colleagues.
